verified_behaviour: The official Cycle 3 hierarchy resolved as River Basin District -> Management Catchment -> Operational Catchment -> Water Body.
The complete reviewed hierarchy contained 10 River Basin Districts, 117 Management Catchments, 750 Operational Catchments and 4929 Water Bodies.
River Basin District GeoJSON supplied 8701 constituent Water Body geometry features for the reviewed snapshot.
Publisher hierarchy relationships were taken from source links rather than inferred spatially.
The complete raw evidence bundle was re-read and normalized successfully before database publication.
The real evidence bundle loaded atomically into a disposable PostGIS database.
An exact-content retry returned the same stored snapshot only after stored child-row and geometry integrity verification.
Stored child counts exactly matched the normalized snapshot counts.

geometry_policy.parent_geometry_note: River Basin District, Management Catchment and Operational Catchment GeoJSON responses contain constituent Water Body features and are not represented as publisher-authored single canonical parent polygons.

rate_policy.throttling_policy: HTTP 403 or 429 is treated as retrieval failure after bounded retries and is never interpreted as an empty hierarchy.

limitations: This is a dated verification of the Cycle 3 public source and does not establish that future publisher inventories or geometry remain unchanged.
WaterGeo does not claim a publisher-supplied Hydrology station-to-catchment relationship.
Any future spatial station-to-catchment relationship must be explicitly labelled as WaterGeo-derived rather than publisher-authored.
Classification, objectives, measures, RNAGS, protected areas and other Catchment Data Explorer datasets are outside this Phase 2C scope.
